questions.q: Why does the impossible-travel incident get worked as a full investigation even at Medium severity?
options: Because two successful sign-ins from different countries forty minutes apart is a strong enough signal to earn a full look, not a quick dismissal
Because every Medium severity incident must be escalated automatically
Because Medium severity incidents never contain entity mappings
Because Sentinel reclassifies all impossible-travel alerts as High after one hour
questions.explain: Severity is a starting point for triage, not the whole judgment — the specific pattern here is serious enough to warrant a full investigation.

questions.q: What does expanding the Account node in the investigation graph show?
options: Every other alert and entity connected to that same user account
Only the single alert that created this incident
A list of all users in the Azure AD tenant
The KQL query that generated the analytics rule
questions.explain: The investigation graph surfaces connections across alerts and entities automatically, which is the direct payoff of the entity mapping configured when the rule was built.

questions.q: What question is the hunting query in this lesson designed to answer?
options: Whether either of the incident's two IP addresses also touched a different user account
Whether the user's password meets complexity requirements
How many Sentinel workbooks exist in the workspace
Whether the analytics rule's schedule needs to change
questions.explain: The hunting query scopes to the incident's own IP addresses and summarizes by account, checking whether the compromise reaches beyond the one flagged user.

questions.q: What does a bookmark preserve, and why does that matter?
options: A saved query and its exact result set, tagged to the incident, so the evidence survives past the current session
A copy of the entire Log Analytics workspace
A permanent change to the analytics rule's threshold
A screenshot of the investigation graph only
questions.explain: Bookmarking the hunting query's result turns a one-time check into documented evidence the next analyst (or the same one, later) can rely on.

questions.q: What is the correct order of steps this lesson walks through for investigating the incident?
options: Open the incident from the queue, read the investigation graph and entity timeline, run a hunting query, add a bookmark
Add a bookmark, then open the incident, then delete the analytics rule
Run a hunting query before the incident exists in the queue
Close the incident immediately without reviewing the graph
questions.explain: The investigation moves from the queue to the graph and timeline, then outward with a hunting query to check scope, ending with a bookmark to preserve the evidence.
